scope: M0/M1 engineering acceptance plan. These are test requirements, not claims of passing tests.

cases.given: Empty SQLite development and PostgreSQL databases
cases.then: One expected revision head; idempotent second execution; no app startup DDL. First slice creates baseline/adoption metadata only; later ownership/artifact/ledger revisions have their own owners. Runtime role cannot CREATE/ALTER/stamp. Fresh install records fresh origin; identical installation-key replay at the same installed revision is a no-op. AR-007-A explicit initialization supplies real project/principal grants; changed key/intent or unknown nonempty DB refuses. Fresh initialization transitions prepared to ownership_complete with non-null targets and still-null inapplicable legacy backup/drain evidence.

cases.given: Known v0.1 fixture with binary artifacts, parent branch and budget values
cases.then: IDs, event hashes, content digests and reservations unchanged. After actual upgrade verify all 14 original rows, 18 ciphertexts and 245000 microUSD opening holds, inherited ancestor identity and separate event/artifact digests. No invented calls or billing.

cases.given: Unknown schema or newer revision
cases.then: Refuse safely with schema_incompatible; no schema writes. Reject changed type/default/nullability/constraint/index or unexpected write-changing trigger/rule, partial schema and multiple heads before DDL. Matching schema plus corrupt history cannot activate.

cases.given: Backfill interrupted mid-batch
cases.when: Resume migration and retry concurrent migrator
cases.then: No duplicated/lost rows; one migrator owns lock; compatibility state explicit. Writer exclusion spans fingerprint through stamp; active/expired running jobs, queued work and an old writer block adoption. Repeating identical mapping is idempotent; changed mapping conflicts. Test kill before/after commit, lock timeout and restore.

cases.given: Runs with equal timestamps and inserts between pages
cases.then: Stable descending (created_at,id), no duplicates, initial watermark honored. Cursor also binds principal/limit/expiry and maximum immutable published_seq, excluding later backfills with older creation time. No artifact reads for list. Commit-order allocation is serialized per project: a delayed insert transaction cannot publish a pre-watermark row after page one; test reversed transaction completion and rollback.

cases.given: Forged or foreign-project cursor
cases.then: 422 invalid_cursor or 404 inaccessible project; no foreign data.

cases.given: Viewer, operator and admin in two projects
cases.then: Viewer cannot mutate; unauthorized IDs return 404; admin action mapping explicit. No implicit default project; issuer+subject identities differ across issuers; old sessions reauthenticate, key role intersects membership, bootstrap cannot read customer data.

cases.given: Previously accepted idempotent request then membership revoked
cases.then: Access denied, no payload/operation IDs leaked from idempotency cache.

cases.given: Foreign study/run/parent/file/key IDs including compare route
cases.then: No authorization bypass through legacy endpoints or nested refs. Require full transitive run/study/job/key/artifact owner closure; second-project activation waits for all legacy routes and nested refs. Workbench keeps rich legacy shapes. Every new legacy run/branch/study/investigate job freezes scoped common config metadata while preserving version1 bodies; missing/drifted config or v2 envelope mismatch blocks paid dispatch; old unmapped jobs never automatically redispatch.

cases.given: Eight concurrent identical requests
cases.then: One job+operation+audit creation; every accepted response returns original IDs. After response loss and native-v1 config/default/image change, resolve existing frozen operation before new upload; storage outage cannot require a different config or operation identity.

cases.given: Same key or client_operation_id with changed request
cases.then: 409 idempotency_conflict; no extra job. Changed request digest, principal or project cannot recover original operation; same-principal current authorization is required. Model config alone is not client-intent drift.

cases.given: Same client_operation_id and body but different keys
cases.then: Same operation; new key is atomically bound as an alias. Reusing that alias with a different client ID/body conflicts; no duplicate job. Composite operation-key FK rejects mismatched project, principal or kind even when operation ID exists.

cases.given: Oversized manifest, bad path or unknown adapter
cases.then: 413/422 and zero admitted jobs; no submitted private contents in error. Reject duplicate keys/nonfinite/bool-as-integer/unknown fields, compressed input outside identity encoding, chunked >9MiB and canonical materialized TaskSpec >8MiB without leaking dynamic file paths.

cases.given: Queued/running/terminal operations
cases.then: Intent idempotent; queued cancelled, running flagged, terminal state preserved.

cases.given: Object write succeeds and metadata transaction fails
cases.then: No broken committed reference; orphan identifiable; no plaintext object. Register complete task/config/envelope and transitive child references; no missing child silently publishes. Measure actual PUT requests and logical writes separately; do not assume cache savings.

cases.given: Corrupt ciphertext/hash or missing object
cases.then: Integrity/missing failure visible; no successful body or fabricated empty snapshot. System namespace cannot expose customer objects; unclassified historical objects stay inaccessible and retained, with no GC or guessed owner.

cases.given: Same bytes in separate projects
cases.then: No existence/read oracle across projects; authorization before cache lookup. Composite artifact reference FKs reject a foreign-project object or owner, with matching unique target keys in the migration.

cases.given: Eight concurrent reservations that jointly exceed a shared cap
cases.then: Only cap-compliant reservations succeed; all account updates commit or none. Reject foreign job/account/evidence even when IDs exist. Opening holds imported once; new reserves counted once per level, with gross jobs.reserved=L+sum(R). Reject project-scope account with NULL project_id (SQL UNKNOWN is not a scope grant), organization account with project/job IDs and job account missing either ID.

cases.given: Expired owner, cancellation, timeout and repeated logical call ID
cases.then: No new reservation after fence/cancel; timeout held; identical logical call not double counted. Test stale owner and generation, cancellation, DB outage, changed logical-call request and crash after reserved->dispatching. Repeated permit lookup cannot dispatch twice; M1 does not promise atomic external HTTP.

cases.given: Billing period changes while a call is uncertain
cases.then: Original admission-period accounts retained; no reset-based cap bypass or automatic release. Unresolved historic and prior-period holds constrain new admission; no rollover reset, automatic settlement, synthetic invoice or timeout release.

cases.given: Database unavailable before permit
cases.then: Fail closed before network dispatch.

cases.given: Provider/storage exceptions include a sentinel secret and source text
cases.then: Safe code+IDs available; sentinel absent from all logs, responses and metric labels. Nested stored failure correlation stays constant across 200 polls while each X-Request-ID is fresh. Legacy detail is fixed safe text; v1 uses four fields.

cases.given: Required database unavailable
cases.then: Liveness indicates process; readiness fails without echoing credentials; no paid call. AR-005-C revision guard is prerequisite. Missing/future/multiple revision, incomplete required phase, oversize/corrupt/missing/slow sentinel, stale success and drain fail readiness. Read <=5561 ciphertext bytes before decrypt, <=4096 plaintext, no customer blob or probe write; total deadline1s/inflight1/cache<=5s.

cases.given: Proposed API/data contracts and historical readers
cases.then: Unresolved refs/incompatible changes fail; deterministic unit+PostgreSQL+existing gVisor gates preserved.

G0: Assumptions and supported workload reviewed with product owner.
Architecture/contract decisions and first implementation slice explicitly approved.
Data rights and spending limits documented; production hiring or spend not presumed.
G1: AR-005 through AR-012 acceptance cases implemented and passing at an identified commit.
Existing historical fixture preserves hashes, bytes and budget accounting.
Scoped legacy and v1 interfaces cannot leak across projects.
No duplicate submission or atomic budget-cap violation under concurrency.
Code review, safe diagnostics, migration/recovery notes and roadmap evidence updated.
